174	
175	Each landed rung's "Revival change" section, both its parts word for word, in the order the rungs landed, with the rows' numbers in place of the placeholders (row 845 in rung C's); no line it cites was moved by the other rung.
176	
177	### C (`rung-natives-compiled`, `98b04d371`)
178	
179	**The change.** The team's library says of `builtinPrimitive` that it "is actually recognized as a special piece of built-in magic by the Fortress interpreter" and that its argument "names a Java Class which is a subclass of `com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp`" (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-17`); walk reads the string only as such a class (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-215`); the compiler has no counterpart, so a compile of such a body says 'Variable builtinPrimitive is not defined.' What the tree now does: on the compiled path, a `builtinPrimitive("pkg.Class.method")` body whose string names a public static method of a class under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` is read at the parse as a call of that method, through a synthetic `import java` of it, `self` first for a method of a trait or object, so the checker checks the declaration against the method's Java signature (`NativeHelperBindingCompiled`, `XXXNativeHelperMisfitCompiled`); a string under that package that names no public static method is a static error, 'builtinPrimitive names no static helper: …' (`XXXNativeHelperMisspeltCompiled`); every other string, the glue classes among them, stays a call of `builtinPrimitive` (`XXXNativeHelperOutsidePackageCompiled`); walk reads every `builtinPrimitive` string as before. In walk's world, the checker reads such a method's Java types as the one library's types (`NamingCzar.java:369-372`, `:464-505`; `NamingCzarJUTest.testForeignOneLibrary`), and so does walk's own reading of a written `import java`, which therefore stops one gap later, at F-180's gap 3 (row 845). The reason: the glue classes take walk's evaluator values, which the compiled path cannot pass (`NativeApp.java:164-215`; the classes under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/`), and the compiled path refused every native binding: 'Variable builtinPrimitive is not defined.' at `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperBindingCompiled.fss:5:32-46` on the base. The compiled path's own binding of a static Java method, `import java`, is the machinery the rewrite goes through (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Compilation.rats:235-239`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/repository/GraphRepository.java:1022-1025`).
180	
181	**Provenance.** P-58, "Every native binding is a `builtinPrimitive` call naming a static helper"; the batch's forks 2 to 5 (the switch per repository, the refusal under the helpers' package, the import collector's hook, the stand-in reading) and 14 (row 309 closed); the rewrite keyed to the helpers' package is this rung's change of the planner's text, by the crash it measured; climb batch 23, rung C.
182	
183	### W (`rung-natives-walk`, `640acb4a1`)
184	
185	#### The change
186	
187	- The team's sources: the comment of `builtinPrimitive` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-29` at the team's last commit `a874948ac`), which the specification prints in its `FortressBuiltin` api, says that the argument "names a Java Class which is a subclass of `com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp`"; walk's `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-215` there) loads the string only with `Class.forName` and refuses anything else, 'Native class … not found.'; and every binding of the team's library names such a glue class, so walk's `ZZ32` `DIV` by zero ends the run in `Int$Div`'s `x / y` (`interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:126`).
188	- What the tree now does: the string names either a glue class or a public static method of a class of `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers`, written `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.Class.method`; walk takes the method whose Java types carry the declared types, `self` first, carries values at the declared types, raises a helper's compiled exception as the library's, and refuses a string under that package that names nothing or fits nothing (`ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperBindingWalk.fss`, `NativeHelperRaiseWalk.fss`, `NativeHelperMisspeltWalk.fss`, `NativeHelperMisfitWalk.fss`, `NativeHelperUncarriedWalk.fss`), though it reads a method's `self` only by its Java type, so a binding in a method of a program's own type loads (`XXXNativeHelperUncarriedSelfWalk.fss`). Trait `ZZ32`'s `=`, `<`, `-`, `DOTMINUS`, `+`, `DOTPLUS`, `DOT`, `TIMES`, juxtaposition, `DOTTIMES`, `DIV`, `BITAND`, `BITOR`, `BITXOR`, `BITNOT`, `widen` and `unsigned`, and `Int`'s `asString` and `asExprString`, name the helpers the compiler's own library binds (`NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk.fss`), and `ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero raises `DivisionByZero` (`ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk.fss`). A helper bound over `String` receives a non-flat string's type name, as a glue class does (`NativeHelperNonFlatStringWalk.fss`).
189	- The reason, as evidence: a glue class takes walk's boxed values, `protected final FValue applyToArgs(FValue x, FValue y)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Util.java:253-254`), which compiled code does not have; the compiled path binds its natives to these same static methods over plain Java values, as `import java com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.{…}` in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`. A binding that names a helper is the one text both paths can call. The helper's raise names a class of the compiled library, `Utility.makeFortressException("fortress.CompilerBuiltin$DivisionByZero")` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java:79`), which walk has not, hence the translation; and the specification asks the exception: "For integer results, division by zero throws a DivisionByZero." (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:164-165`).
190

193	P-58 (item 35, the curator's answer of 10 October 2026: `builtinPrimitive` naming a static helper, a loader beside the glue classes on walk); question 2 of climb batch 23, answered option 1 (the first family moves in this rung); climb batch 23's forks 6 to 15 (overload by declared types, values at declared types, `self` first, the dotted method by arity, refusal at load, the raise translation, the family of 21, row 336 rewritten, rows 796 and 309 closed, the comment revised by this rung); climb batch 23, rung W, rung-natives-walk.

check: contains, does_not_contain, equals, matches,
                               WIcontains (containment with runs of whitespace collapsed)

A `run` fails if the program exits non-zero or a `run_*` check fails. With no `run_out` check, its output must contain `pass` or `PASS`. For example:

    tests=EqualityRung1
    link
    run
    run_out_WIcontains=PASS

## How `XXX` works

- Under walk, an `XXX` test is `tests/XXXName.fss`, whose component is `XXXName`. With no `.test` file, it is green when it fails as a plain test would.
- In the compiled test folders, the `XXX` prefix of a `.test` file's name applies to every command that the file drives: each must fail. So a defect at run time, whose link succeeds, needs two `.test` files ("Writing an `XXX` test").
- An unmet `run_*` check makes a run test red, whatever the prefix.
- The harness reports any link or compile exception of a component whose name contains `XXX` as expected, whatever the `.test` file's name. Only an unmet key of that command makes it red.
- An `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key, whose program compiles, reports "Saw wrong failure", which is red.
- A green `XXX` test prints `Saw expected failure` or `OK Saw expected exception`.

## How a defect is recorded

Record every defect that you measure in one of three ways, and say in your report which:

1. Your change repairs it: an assertion in your plain gated test. It needs no `XXX` stage.
2. It is deferred, and the specification settles it: a gated `XXX` test that asserts the specification's answer. Write it in the change that measured the defect, even if a later change will repair it. A deferred defect of a program that the checker accepts and that then fails the JVM's verification (`VerifyError`), linkage or a range check at run time is one of these.
3. It is deferred, and the specification is silent or a conflict leaves it open (`exploring.md`): a test that asserts today's behaviour, and a row in the gap ledger (`records.md`). If no program can observe the defect, or no gated test can pass while it shows, as when walk crashes on the program, write the ledger row only. Its reproducer, the row's cell that names the test, is `none`, and its notes give the command and its output.

If your brief does not let you edit the original tree, say in your report which of the three the defect needs, and write a ledger row for it, whichever it needs. A probe that only measures and reports is an example. The change that next works there writes the test.

## The order: the test, its failure, the fix, the pass

1. Write the test, with a plain name. Write the essence of the defect as a clean, minimal program, not the shape in which a probe met it.
2. See the test fail through the harness (`harness-one.sh` or `junit.sh`, `tests-running.md`) on the base's code. Do this in a run that ends before you first build or compile your edit. Under walk, do it before you edit a library source that the test reads. If your tree already holds the fix, run the test through the harness on the old code, as `worktrees.md`, "Running the old code", says.
3. Make the fix. See the test pass in your last run after your last change of code.

The test needs no commit of its own. A test that comes with no fix, such as one that guards a behaviour that works today, has no failing run: see it pass through the harness.

In your report, quote two to five lines of the failing run, if there is one, and the passing line, each with its command. In an edit of the original tree, put every check into a gated test, never into a one-off script. A probe that only measures may use its own script. Assert a value with `assert` in an interpreter test. In a compiled test, assert it with `assert` (above), or print it and check it with a `run_out_equals` key. The harness checks both, so they are part of the suite's verdict.

An edit of prose in `Specification/` or `Documentation/` has no test. Check it as `specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", says.

## Writing an `XXX` test

In a compiled test folder, name the component `XXXName`, in its file `XXXName.fss` and in its `component` line.

- For a refusal at compile time, write one `XXX` compile test, with `compile` and `compile_err_contains=<the refusal's message>`.
- For a code-generator wall (`compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet"), write `XXXName.test` with `tests=XXXName`, `compile` and `compile_exception_contains=<text of the exception>`.
- For a program that compiles and fails at run time, write two `.test` files over the component:
  - `NameLink.test`, a plain name, with `tests=XXXName` and `link`. It is red if the link reports static errors, but green on an exception.
  - `XXXName.test`, with `tests=XXXName` and `run`, and no `link`. Its run uses the plain file's link, so run the two files in one call of `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`, the plain one first.
  - The program prints `REACHED` in `run()` before the part that fails. The `XXX` file checks it with `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or with `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` if the run dies before `run()` prints. Never use `run_out_contains=PASS`.
  - Example: `compiler_tests/XXXBoxDotSpellingsRungW.test` and `BoxDotSpellingsRungWLink.test`.

Show the first `XXX` test that your change adds, and only the first, working through the harness (`harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`), from its place in a gated test folder. A direct compile and run does not show this. Run it twice:

1. As it is: the harness must report an expected failure.
2. Changed for one run so that the defect does not show, then restored: the harness must report it red. For example, add the missing declaration to the test program, set the expected string to what the run prints, or, in a run-time pair, remove the part that fails.

## Promoting an `XXX` test

If your change fixes a defect that has a gated `XXX` test, the fix turns that test red. To find such a test, search the gap ledger (`records.md`): a row's reproducer names it. Also list the `XXX` files: `git ls-files 'ProjectFortress/*XXX*'`. Then promote it:

1. Before you edit the code, remove the prefix: give the test a plain name by its topic. Rename each file with `git mv` (`committing.md` gives the commit), or with `mv` if the file is not committed yet. Rename each `XXX` name inside: the `component` line, and in a compiled test the `tests=` lines and keys. Change a run-time pair as below.
2. See the plain-named test fail through the harness on the base's code, as "The order", step 2, says.
3. Make the fix and see the test pass.

A run-time pair keeps its three files, renamed without `XXX`. For example, `compiler_tests/NatRtTask` was promoted so in `fd5cb4864`:

- `Name.fss`, with `component Name`. The program asserts its values, then prints `PASS` last.
- `NameLink.test`: `tests=Name` and `link`.
- `Name.test`, in place of `XXXName.test`: `tests=Name`, `link`, `run` and `run_out_contains=PASS`.

## Names, comments, citations

- Name a test by its topic. Give it one comment line that says what it checks, with no pointer to a record.
- In a test, cite the specification by file and section or entry, never by line: `opr-overview.tex, subsection "GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators"`. In the library chapters, name the entry too: `basic-integers.tex, section "Integers", opr CHOOSE`.
- If your change breaks a line of a test that the team wrote, respell the line and keep the value that it checks. Keep every assertion. List each line's before and after in your report.
- If your change touches mutable state, a field, an `atomic` block or library code that writes shared state, run its checks at one thread and at four. The same holds for the Java of tasks, transactions or the class loader. `harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` and the suites force four threads. For one thread, run the program directly with the prefix `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` (a compiled program: `compiler.md`, "Running"), and check its exit code and output.

(* On the compiled path, a builtinPrimitive body whose string names a static helper of nativeHelpers compiles into a call of that helper, self first for a method. *)
component NativeHelperBindingCompiled
export Executable

less(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")

trait Shape
  same(self, other:Shape):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
  sameAs(other:Shape, self):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
end

object Box(v:ZZ32) extends Shape
  kind():JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.typeName")
end

add(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intOverflowingAdd")

bazS(s:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")
bazI(n:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")

run():() = do
  assert(less(1, 2), "less(1, 2)")
  assert(NOT less(3, 2), "less(3, 2)")
  b = Box(3)
  c = Box(4)
  assert(same(b, b), "same(b, b)")
  assert(NOT same(b, c), "same(b, c)")
  assert(sameAs(b, b), "sameAs(b, b)")
  assert(NOT sameAs(c, b), "sameAs(c, b)")
  assert(b.kind() = "Box", "b.kind()")
  assert(add(2, 3), 5, "add(2, 3)")
  r: ZZ32 := 0
  try
    r := add(2147483647, 1)
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => r := 1
  end
  assert(r, 1, "add(2147483647, 1) raises IntegerOverflow")
  assert(bazS("x".asJavaString) = "baz x", "bazS")
  assert(bazI(7) = "baz 7", "bazI")
  println("PASS")
end

end

(* Under walk, a builtinPrimitive body whose string names a static helper of nativeHelpers runs that helper, its arguments and result carried at the declared types. *)
component NativeHelperBindingWalk
export Executable

less(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")
plus(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleDoubleArith.doubleAdd")
ladd(a:ZZ64, b:ZZ64):ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleLongArith.longOverflowingAdd")
both(a:Boolean, b:Boolean):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleBoolean.booleanAnd")
cat(a:String, b:String):String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeConcatenate")
len(a:String):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")
wide(a:ZZ64):ZZ = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.makeZZfromZZ64")
nn(a:ZZ32):NN32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedIntArith.makeNN32FromZZ32WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN32ResultType")
ch(a:ZZ32):Char = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charMakeCharacterWithSpecialCompilerHackForCharacterResultType")
code(c:Char):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charCodePointWithSpecialCompilerHackForCharacterArgumentType")
upper(c:Char):Char = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charToUpperCase")
bazS(s:String):String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")
bazI(n:ZZ32):String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")

run():() = do
  assert(less(1, 2), true, "less(1, 2)")
  assert(less(3, 2), false, "less(3, 2)")
  assert(plus(2.5, 3.0), 5.5, "plus(2.5, 3.0)")
  x: ZZ64 = 4000000000
  assert(ladd(x, x), 8000000000, "ladd")
  assert(both(true, false), false, "both")
  assert(cat("ab", "cd"), "abcd", "cat")
  assert(len("abcde"), 5, "len")
  assert(wide(x) wide(x), 16000000000000000000, "wide")
  assert(nn(7), unsigned(7), "nn(7)")
  assert(ch(65), 'A', "ch(65)")
  assert(code('a'), 97, "code('a')")
  assert(upper('q'), 'Q', "upper('q')")
  assert(bazS("x"), "baz x", "bazS")
  assert(bazI(7), "baz 7", "bazI")
end

(* ZZ32's and Int's operators bound to nativeHelpers keep their values and their IntegerOverflow under walk. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk
export Executable

overflows(f: () -> ZZ32): Boolean =
  try
    f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
  end

run():() = do
  a: ZZ32 = 2147483647
  b: ZZ32 = -2147483647 - 1
  m: ZZ32 = -1
  assert(3 = 3, true, "=")
  assert(3 = 4, false, "= unequal")
  assert(3 < 4, true, "<")
  assert(4 < 3, false, "< not")
  assert(-a, -2147483647, "unary -")
  assert(overflows(fn () => -b), "unary - of the minimum overflows")
  assert(DOTMINUS b, b, "unary DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert(a - 1 + 1, a, "+")
  assert(overflows(fn () => a + 1), "+ overflows")
  assert(a DOTPLUS 1, b, "DOTPLUS wraps")
  assert(b + 1 - 1, b, "-")
  assert(overflows(fn () => b - 1), "- overflows")
  assert(b DOTMINUS 1, a, "DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert(46340 DOT 46340, 2147395600, "DOT")
  assert(overflows(fn () => 65536 DOT 65536), "DOT overflows")
  assert(7 TIMES 6, 42, "TIMES")
  assert(overflows(fn () => 65536 TIMES 65536), "TIMES overflows")
  assert(7 6, 42, "juxtaposition")
  assert(overflows(fn () => 65536 65536), "juxtaposition overflows")
  assert(65536 DOTTIMES 65536, 0, "DOTTIMES wraps")
  assert(7 DIV 2, 3, "DIV")
  assert((-7) DIV 2, -3, "DIV rounds toward zero")
  assert(overflows(fn () => b DIV m), "DIV of the minimum by -1 overflows")
  assert(12 BITAND 10, 8, "BITAND")
  assert(12 BITOR 10, 14, "BITOR")
  assert(12 BITXOR 10, 6, "BITXOR")
  assert(BITNOT 12, -13, "BITNOT")
  assert(widen(a).asString, "2147483647", "widen")
  assert(unsigned(m).asString, "4294967295", "unsigned")
  assert(a.asString, "2147483647", "asString")
  assert(b.asExprString, "-2147483648", "asExprString")
  assert(asFloat(m), -1.0, "asFloat")
end

(* ZZ32's DIV by zero throws DivisionByZero, which a catch sees; opr-overview.tex, section "Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators". *)
component ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk
export Executable

dividesByZero(f: () -> ZZ32): Boolean =

    false
  catch e
    DivisionByZero => true
  end

  seven: ZZ32 = 7

end

+- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). A native bound to a helper of `nativeHelpers/` raises the library's own exception where the helper raises a class of the compiled prelude, such as `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$DivisionByZero`, so `ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero raises `DivisionByZero` (F-299). Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes, so a division by zero elsewhere ends the run (rows 336, 848). Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, and for a helper by `tests/NativeHelperRaiseWalk.fss` and `tests/ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk.fss`. The compiled path calls static helpers over plain Java values instead, in `nativeHelpers/`. Matched against those helpers, the 424 bindings were: 147 whose operation the compiler's prelude already binds to a helper at the same owner and signature, so only the binding's string changes, to name that helper (P-58); 61 whose helper exists, but no binding names it under that name and signature, 25 of them under a name that the compiler's prelude gives to another helper, such as the 12 wrapping operators (row 348); 138 that need a new helper; and 78 that need more, 36 methods of native I/O objects and 42 with no compiled analogue. Since the count, `9d2e4c856` (2026-10-02) made 24 more `IntLiteral` bindings in `FortressBuiltin.fss` live: the five conversions `asZZ32` to `asZZ`, and the 19 operators that had stood inside a comment. They are not classified. At `3cd653815` the library had 449 live bindings, all naming glue classes; 21 of them now name a helper of `nativeHelpers/` (F-299), and 428 still name glue classes. Every program's output needs `Writer`'s natives, among the 36 I/O methods, since `println` writes through a native `Writer`. MicroGPT also needs `nanoTime`, which needs a new helper, since the compiled one returns `RR64`; `getProgramArgsPrim`, which `System` calls as it loads; and `NativeArray`. The last two have no compiled analogue. The 42 with no analogue: `NativeArray` waits for the array decision on how a float vector's `double[]` store goes (P-85), and `Thread`, `Reflect` and `printTaskTrace` are off microGPT's path. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` section 2.
+- F-298 **A `builtinPrimitive` body whose string names a static helper of `nativeHelpers/` compiles on the compiled path as a call of that helper.** At the parse, on every repository but walk's (`Shell.specificRepository`, `Shell.java:102-103`), a body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("pkg.Class.method")`, its string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` and naming a public static method, becomes a call through a synthetic `import java` of the helper, `self` first for a method of a trait or object, so the checker checks the declaration against the helper's Java signature (P-58; `compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:46-64`, `:87-123`; `compiler/Parser.java:157-159`, `:329-330`). ## The specification

The callout `\revision{revival-native-helpers}{…}` stands in the comment: the api's typesetting carries it, the PDF printing the box under the first paragraph ('REVISED BY THE 2026 REVIVAL', 'SEE', 'Section I.1.44', `pdftotext` of the built PDF).
- Appendix I, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, the entry "A native binding that names a static helper", before "Passages not yet revised": affected section `\secref{FortressBuiltin}`; the change; the rationale, the decision of 10 October 2026 (P-58), the way not taken (`import java` in the library) and the reversal, with the decision record's path; the effect: the 21 bindings, the 428 on glue classes, `CHOOSE` (row 521), the compiled code checking but not yet running them until the switch-over, `ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero now as the operators chapter says, and `REM`, `MOD`, `ZZ64`'s three and `ZZ`'s `DIV` still ending the run (row 336), the natives over `String` (row 846); the original text quoted from the `.fsi`, since `Specification-1.0-frozen/library/default-libraries.tex:39` inputs a generated `library/apis/FortressBuiltin.tex` that neither tree keeps (the build typesets it, `Specification/fortress/build.xml:129-139`); route C the same.
- `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:54-64`: still true (it describes the revision in general); not edited.
- The build: `cd Specification/fortress && ./ant genSource && ./ant tex`, both 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', and the count of reference, label and undefined-control-sequence warnings 0, on the comment's final text; once more after two phrasings of the entry's rationale changed (the library macro with a possessive), both 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', warnings 0, the entry typeset as 'I.1.44 A native binding that names a static helper'. The build's files removed (`git clean -fXq -- Specification`).
- Other sentences of `Specification/` on these topics (`grep -rn -i 'builtinPrimitive\|native component\|nativeHelpers\|division by zero\|DivisionByZero' Specification --include=*.tex`): `opr-overview.tex:164-165`, now true for `ZZ32`'s `DIV` under walk; `basic/components/source-code.tex:513-518`, untouched; `appendices/changes.tex:2473`, a past refusal of calls of `builtinPrimitive` (row 560), still true as written; `basic/evaluation/completion.tex:29-31` and the number chapters, on `/` and `QQ`, untouched.

## Sentences made false

- `Specification/`: none outside the revised comment, whose original Appendix I keeps.
- POSITIONS P-58: "Every binding still names a glue class." (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:55`): 21 name helpers.
- FACTS F-24 (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:18`, the skeptic's addition): "Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes, so a division by zero ends the run (row 336).": `ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero raises `DivisionByZero`.
- FACTS F-32 (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:28`): its count is of glue bindings; 428 of the 449 live bindings now name glue classes, 21 helpers. F-180 (`FACTS.md:243`): "P-58 chose another way, not yet built": walk's half is built.

- The skill: `interpreter.md`, "Natives": "The library binds each of walk's natives by a string in its `.fss` files: `builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.X")`. The classes are in `interpreter/glue/prim/`." (21 now name helpers), and "A `catch` sees no other Java exception, so any other exception from a native ends the run, a division by zero too." (`ZZ32`'s `DIV` raises `DivisionByZero`, and a helper's compiled raise is translated); `library.md`, "Designing a change": "A new native is a Java class under `interpreter/glue/prim/` …" (a native can be a helper of `nativeHelpers/`).

### Forks the batch takes, none consequential

Each default can be undone, and none reverses a decision of yours or touches a line of microGPT.

1. **Two rungs, C and W; W lands only with C.** Default: so. W does not build on C: its walk tests pass on its own tree, where the checker reads the moved strings as calls of `builtinPrimitive`, as it reads every glue string (row 560). P-58's check of them needs C's rewrite, so W lands only where C does. The gather applies C, then W.
2. **The rewrite's switch: on while the compiled path's repository is in use, off under walk's.** Default: `Shell.specificRepository` turns it on for the analyzed-cache repository and off for the interpreter's, so the compile commands, `fortress junit` and the gate's two stages rewrite, and walk does not. The binding probe left the key open between the compiled world, which would hide every moved binding from the gate's stages until N5, and the command (`natives-binding-probe.md`, "Questions for the curator"). P-58's "from the step that moves a binding" settles it for the command. Both stages call `Shell.compilerPhases` (`coordinator/tools/distance/DistanceMulti.java`, `checker-count/WorldFlip.java`), so no tool changes. Walk reads its own parsed cache (`interpreter_parsed_cache/`), so no rewritten tree reaches it.
3. **The refusal.** Default: a string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` that names no public static method is a static error at the string, 'builtinPrimitive names no static helper: …'; every other string that names no such method is left alone, glue strings among them, whose class part is a package. The rewrite itself takes any string that names a public static method of a class that loads, and only the refusal is keyed to the helpers' package (`BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.fn` in `rung-C.patch`); on the base every string names a glue class, so none is rewritten. That is the binding probe's rule ("So the landing rung needs one more rule", section 1), from which P-58's "refuse a string that names no helper" was written. Refusing glue strings too would refuse all 428 left on the compiled path before they move.
4. **The import collector's hook only for a component whose text names a helper.** Default: so. The repository learns of a synthetic `import java` only from the import collector's view of the file (`GraphRepository.readCUFor`), so that view must be the rewritten component. content.content: - P-58 **Every native binding is a `builtinPrimitive` call naming a static helper.** A native binding is a library body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("…")`, the library's own form, and it keeps that form. Why: the language has no foreign-function interface, only a planned one, so the library's own practice decides the binding's form. Its string is to name a static Java method in `nativeHelpers/`, the compiled path's helpers, such as `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT"`, in place of a glue class of walk, which the compiled path cannot use (F-32). Walk is to load the named helper through a loader beside its glue classes. At the parse, before the checker, the compiled path is to rewrite each such body into a synthetic `import java` of the helper and a call, and to refuse a string that names no helper. The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and from the step that moves a binding, the compiled checker checks it against the helper's Java signature, not all at once at the switch-over. The other form, `import java` declarations written in the library itself, is not taken. Every binding still names a glue class. Row 796: walk loads a binding's string only as a glue class. # Plan: microGPT compiled on the JVM

The order Pavol approved on 2026-09-26 (P-33). The evidence under it is the inventory `coordinator/open-items-2026-09-26.md`.

## Where we stand

- **Runs.** microGPT runs under walk. - **Stops.** On the compiled path all 18 of microGPT's components stop at name resolution, as expected until the switch-over; the ladder-regression stage holds them at that phase (FACTS, The harness and the gate).
- **The live thread.** One library, the interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks. At the last landed gate, climb batch 22c's (`b81d86b75`), the distance is 0 and the checker count 0, '#crash none', now over the fourteen components, the twelve prelude components and the two that `List` imports, under the compile command's own setting (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-22c/gate/`; F-53, F-288, F-289). Its four rungs: the export check reads every top-level symbolic operator, the library's 9 headers matched (rung O; P-155; rows 782 and 827), and counts every api member, the component declaring the 12 that its api writes `abstract`, with the specification's export rule revised (rung A; P-158, F-297; row 816); `List`'s two imports are cleared and checked (rung L; F-288; rows 828 and 829); and `fortress compile` bounds a type parameter written without a bound by `Any`, as walk does (rung B; P-42, F-296; rows 412 and 759). The count stage took about 170 s and the distance stage 238 s there (F-240). Its tables and `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, its header alone, are the next batch's comparands. The zero rests on one reading he has not confirmed: the export check compares an object's value parameter less `var`, where the export rule asks the same header (row 844; gather.1 under "Climb batch 22c, listed for his review"); the check's stricter readings hide nothing, and row 839's laxer one hides nothing in the fourteen by a read of their text (`reviews/batch-22c-review.md`, section 6). The library's other components are cleared as the need arises, `System` by the switch-over (P-33); climb batch 23's planner checked those that microGPT imports, report-only: 31 errors, `System`'s 2 among them (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-23.md`, section 1, "What the batch leaves out"). What each batch moved is in its record (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/RECORD.md`) and its review (`reviews/batch-*-review.md`); the earlier texts of this section are in `microgpt-run-c-handover-history.md` and, from 2026-10-15, `coordinator/PLAN-history.md`.

The skill writer's second task, with the review's Part 3, its cold read and the writer's fixes come before climb batch 23 is launched (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "After the landing: the coordinator's routing", steps 4 and 5). Then climb batch 23, phase 4's first batch, the natives' mechanism with N1's first family (phase 4's first line), on his go of 22:36:37 UTC on 2026-10-29, its record re-checked on the new base (`c1a7c7eb0`). What is in flight is `coordinator/BOOT.md`.

## The principle for the batches

Every batch lands with the specification, the library and both paths agreeing. So the work is grouped by what has to change together, not split finer.

Two rules of the batch machinery shape the order: two rungs in one batch may not change the same declaration, and a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch, since every rung branches from the batch's base (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:465`, batch rule 1). That is why the wrapping operators and the flattening sit in different batches, and why rung O's check follows the operators.

How a phase-3 batch's content is chosen (the coordinator's method, as batch 10 was planned): the measure is the distance, the compiled checker's errors on the one library, and the source is the last landed gate's per-site list (`compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`), every error with its site and class. The planner, an Opus worker, sorts it into three piles: (1) decided and free to fix, the library's one-off slips and the checker's defects with a known fix, which go into the batch; (2) waiting on a decision of Pavol's or a judgement (after batch 9: the arrays, 98, after the switch-over by his answer to batch 8's Q4; the self-typed bodies, 30, a list of ways and a judgement first; `isLeftZero` and items 37 to 42, his), which are held and listed in the record; (3) waiting on a probe, which is probed before the record is written (P1 for row 424's F-bounded half). Pile 1 gains the defects the last review routed as owed, the items this plan queues ("a checker rung after batch 8"), and his decisions ready to build (item 20). The pile is cut into rungs by code area, no two rungs on one declaration and none building on another (the two rules above), usually four, since one landing pays for them all and the harness runs two agents at once. Fable reviews the record in place; a question goes to Pavol only where a pile-2 item needs his word. There is no target size and no target cost per error: the planner takes what of pile 1 fits the rungs (batch 10: 148 of the 340, 192 held).

It launches after climb batch 22c's skill steps (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "After the landing: the coordinator's routing", steps 4 and 5).
- The natives (`perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md`, R5), first in the phase by P-33's order, and the third of the three steps that `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` named (F-61). The compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes, the Java classes that the bindings name (F-32, whose count of 424 is from `e455ccd98`). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

content.content:
## Sentences made false

- Specification: none. Appendix I's row 560 entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2465-2476`) speaks of the glue strings' calls of `builtinPrimitive`, which stay. The library's printed comment on `builtinPrimitive` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-17`, typeset by `Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:37-39`) says the function "is actually recognized as a special piece of built-in magic by the Fortress interpreter" and that its argument "names a Java Class which is a subclass of `com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp`". It stays true of every library string on this tree, where none names a helper; it is not true of a compiled program's string that names a helper, as the binding test's, which the compiled path now reads. Rung W revises the comment.
- The record, for the gather: F-180's "P-58 chose another way, not yet built": the compiled half is built here. F-180's "five gaps stop it": the foreign-type reading of walk's world closes gap 1, the type table, for walk itself too, so a written `import java` under walk stops at gap 3 (SKEPTIC.md; row 845 in `record.md`). F-111's "The library names walk's natives only in strings, which only walk resolves": true on this tree, where no library string names a helper; false on the merged tree, where the stages resolve W's moved strings through this rewrite.

## Limits, by reading, not measured

- A component that imports a DSL grammar and names a helper: the import collector's hook parses it whole without its grammar (`Parser.java:157-159`), and `macroParse`'s grammar path, `parseWithGrammars` (`Parser.java:135`), does not apply the rewrite. No library or test component does both: on this tree only three of my four tests hold a helper string (`grep -rl '"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.' --include=*.fss --include=*.fsi .`).
- On the compiled path's repository a component whose text names a helper is parsed whole four times for one analysis: the graph's visitor reads its imports and its exports through `nodeToComponent` (`GraphRepository.java:301`, `:313`), each a `readCUFor` (`:448-451`, `:1022-1025`) while the node holds no component, then `macroParse`'s import collector (`Parser.java:117`) and its `parseFileConvertExn` (`Parser.java:132`); a component that names no helper is parsed whole once, as on the base. On this tree no library file names a helper, so the stages pay nothing; on the merged tree `FortressLibrary.fss` and `FortressBuiltin.fss` do.
- The switch is one static flag, set by the repository made last in a JVM (`Shell.java:103`). `fortress parse` and `fortress api` parse without a repository (`Shell.java:561`, `:702`), so they show no rewrite.

## Points to report

Each is reversible; none holds the push.

1. **The planner's text, changed** (Decision 1): the rewrite keyed to the helpers' package (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:95`), for the crash measured on the text ('java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Undefined API: java.lang'); the varargs test before the alias (`:105`); no provenance in the comments (`:14-33`, `NamingCzar.java:464-468`); the binding test's `sameAs(other:Shape, self)` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperBindingCompiled.fss:9`). Fork 3's description of the text, "The rewrite itself takes any string that names a public static method of a class that loads", no longer holds; its default, the refusal keyed to the package, does.
2. **The tests before and after, through `junit.sh`**: on the base 'Tests run: 4,  Failures: 4,  Errors: 0' (the three planner tests); on the final code 'OK (5 tests)' (with the guard). The guard: red on the planner's text, green on the base and on the final code.
3. **The tables on the final tree**: the count table equal to climb batch 22c's, `diff` printing nothing, '#total 0', '#locations 0', '#crash none'; the count stage 155 s; the distance '#total 0', '#crash none', 'DISTANCE SAME   0' against climb batch 22c's table, 205 s. No site came.
4. **The suites on the final tree**: `ant testQuick` and `ant testSystem` 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL'. The verdicts that change: the five new cases, each green; no other.
5. **A parse of a file that names no helper, and the compiled tests**: no such parse changes. The import collector's hook fires only for a file whose text holds `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` (`Parser.java:157-159`), which on this tree only three of my tests do; the rewrite touches only a string under that package (`BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:95`) and returns the unit itself when it rewrites nothing (`:52`). No compiled test but my own changed its verdict (`ant testQuick` above), and the five glue-string programs of the ladder subset kept their phase and first error.
6. **Sentences made false**: none of the specification; the library's comment on `builtinPrimitive` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-17`) for a compiled program's helper string, not for any library string; F-180's "not yet built" and, on the merged tree, F-111's "which only walk resolves" ("Sentences made false").
7. **Files beyond those named**: a fourth test pair, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXNativeHelperOutsidePackageCompiled.fss` and `.test`, in the named folder beyond the three named tests (Decision 8). No edit of `interpreter/`, `Library/`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`, `nativeHelpers/`, `scala_src/` or the tools: `git diff --name-only 3cd653815 HEAD` lists the eight test files and `Shell.java`, `compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java`, `compiler/NamingCzar.java`, `compiler/Parser.java`.

## Competing names

`grep -rl` over `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress`, `ProjectFortress/tests`, `ProjectFortress/*_tests`, `Library` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` for each name the change adds (`BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter`, `builtinPrimitive_`, `NativeHelperBindingCompiled`, `NativeHelperMisfitCompiled`, `NativeHelperMisspeltCompiled`, `NativeHelperOutsidePackageCompiled`, `oneLibraryTypeForForeignJavaType`, `oneLibraryForeignJavaTranslations`, `namesHelpers`, `namesStaticMethod`, 'names no static helper') finds only the change's own files; `sameAs` is declared nowhere in the compiler's library (`Library/Compiler*.fs?`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fs?`, `AnyType.fs?`).

## Decisions

1. **The planner's text, changed in four places.** Ways not taken: the text as it is; the binding probe's own class. (a) The rewrite keyed to the helpers' package, not any loadable class's public static method: the measured crash and the binding above; walk's loader keys to the same package (`rung-W.patch`, `StaticNativeApp.isHelperString`); P-58: "Its string is to name a static Java method in `nativeHelpers/`". The way not taken with it: keep the text's wide rewrite and widen the hook's test to every string that names a static method, which would make `builtinPrimitive` a general Java binding on the compiled path that walk refuses, and cost a reflective lookup of each of the 449 glue strings at every graph build. Fork 3's own default, the refusal keyed to the package, is kept. (b) The varargs test before the alias is registered: the text registered the alias and then left the declaratio
2. **The switch per repository** (fork 2). Ways not taken: keyed to the compiler's world, which hides every moved binding from the stages until N5; the probe's `-Dfortress.builtinPrimitive.rewrite` property.
3. **The refusal only under the helpers' package** (fork 3). Way not taken: refuse every string that names no helper, which would refuse every glue string on the compiled path before it moves.
4. **The import collector's hook only for a file whose text names a helper** (fork 4). Way not taken: the probe's whole parse of every component there.
5. **The stand-in reading in `NamingCzar`'s three-argument form** (fork 5). Way not taken: natives-shape's gap 1 patch, which rewrote the table at class load and failed `NamingCzarJUTest.testForeign` in the planner's run.
6. **A declaration with a varargs parameter left alone**, as the text does. Way not taken: refuse a helper string on such a declaration. No library binding with a varargs parameter names a helper: the three, `Library/Reflect.fss:313`, `:319`, `:389`, name glue classes over walk's `Type` objects.
7. **Only the tight juxtaposition matched**, not walk's one-item `MathPrimary` branch (`NativeApp.java:175-182`): the parser turns a one-item `MathPrimary` into a tight juxtaposition (`Expression.rats:468-471`, `ExprFactory.simplifyMathPrimary` at `ExprFactory.java:2053-2056`), and the rewrite runs on the parser's tree. Way not taken: match both shapes, as walk does after the phases.
8. **The guard as an `XXX` compile test asserting 'Variable builtinPrimitive is not defined.'**, the form of every compile-error test in `compiler_tests/` (fork 18). Ways not taken: the fix with no test; a new refusal of a string outside the package, which fork 3 does not take. At N5, when the one library declares `builtinPrimitive`, the guard's message changes, and N5 reads it.
9. **The ladder subset: the five files whose recorded first error names `builtinPrimitive`** in the baseline's `ladder.tsv` (`explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/ladder.tsv`): `tests/XXXarityTestFn.fss`, `XXXfailTestFn.fss`, `XXXnoclassNativeFn.fss`, `nativeTestFn.fss`, `testPrim.fss`, all glue strings. No other first error names what the change touched: the parse, the import collector and the foreign-type reading in walk's world.

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

## 1. Syntax: lexing, expressions and declarations

The parser and walk's reading of program text: tokens, operator words and reserved words, subscripts and superscripts after a primary, and the declaration forms with their naming and shadowing rules.

| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `x[i][j]` and `x[i]^2` are grammatical, but walk invokes a subscript followed by a subscript or a superscript without its first index: one index fails with `args = ()`, more silently give the wrong element | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk) | `appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex`, "Expressions"; `basic/operators/precedence.tex`, "Operator Precedence and Associativity"; `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition" | none | astra, blinded, review | Such a primary parses as a `MathPrimary` (not `SubscriptExpr`); `Evaluator.java:1052` sends its subscript to `evalAndInvokeMethod`, whose `evalInvocationArgs` (`Evaluator.java:1251-1252`) takes `exprs.subList(1,…)`, right for a juxtaposition list and wrong for a subscript list. `m[3,7]^2` silently prints `11449`, `(m[7])^2`, not `1075369` (`explorations/gap-ledger-probes/g02.fss`). A library met it too: `rs[k][j]`
| 2 | a subscript of two indices then a superscript, `m[3,7]^2`, silently evaluates `(m[7])^2` under walk | DUPLICATE | implementation gap (walk) | `appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex`, "Expressions" | none | gap ledger merge | duplicate of row 1. Probe `explorations/gap-ledger-probes/g03.fss`, in the parent of `e879b6a44`. |
